answer: For a bridge survey across karst terrain, an agent called ivory earns bidding rights only by completing unpredictable, time-limited test jobs. Each identity receives a different input after committing, and must post a refundable bond per active job. Auditors compare signed measurements with hidden control points; fabricated results forfeit the bond. A hundred aliases must fund a hundred bonds and solve a hundred distinct tests before deadlines, so copying one successful transcript cannot multiply cheap identities.
